title: Inference cache consistency: customer status update and remediation commitments
content:
Executive summary:

We observed a regionally correlated set of customer reports (primarily EU-west and us-east-1) where model responses were intermittently inconsistent for repeated identical requests. Symptoms included: truncated outputs on retry, duplicated final tokens, and seemingly stale context leading to incorrect answers for prompt sequences that relied on recent keys. Impact window: ~2027-03-01 22:30 UTC to 2027-03-02 06:15 UTC. Customers may have seen increased 5xx rates and returned responses that did not reflect their most recent prompts.

What customers experienced (concise for status page):
- Periodic incorrect or stale results for repeated identical requests
- Elevated error rate on some routes during the window
- Partial responses followed by abrupt truncation on retries

Scope & affected customers:
- Not limited to a single account; surfaced in multiple customers that use multi-turn chat and long-context models.
- No evidence of PII exfiltration or unauthorized data access.
- Estimated ~0.6% of hosted requests across the affected regions during the window.

Immediate actions we took (already implemented):
- Rolled back an experimental cache invalidation optimization (RWI-2981) that reduced KV eviction signaling across the serving mesh. Rollback completed by 2027-03-02 01:10 UTC.
- Temporarily disabled cross-region request routing for latency-optimized routes to ensure local KV cache coherence (completed 2027-03-02 02:00 UTC).
- Activated conservative retry behavior server-side: on detected cache-mismatch errors we now return a 409-style response to prompt clients to retry once, rather than auto-resending with partial KV state (rolled out 02:45 UTC).
- Notified customers via status page and direct email to affected account contacts.

Root cause (what we believe happened):
- A recent serving runtime change attempted to accelerate cache invalidation by sending a reduced set of eviction signals to downstream workers for performance reasons. Under certain request-ordering interleavings at high concurrency, some workers missed key TTL/eviction messages and served stale KV cache entries for subsequent requests.
- The stale entries were small (prefix/kvs for a user session) but enough to change token selection in later decoding, producing incorrect/stale responses.
- This condition was amplified by the combination of: 1) heavy workload with many short-lived sessions, 2) cross-region routing (requests landing on workers without fresh invalidation signals), and 3) the new optimization that decreased heartbeat/invalidation bandwidth.

Why this was not captured by existing monitors:
- Our per-token latency and aggregate error-rate monitors were within expected ranges for short periods, and the root cause produced subtle semantic errors rather than large-scale HTTP 5xx spikes initially.
- We lacked a lightweight KV-invalidation telemetry signal in the public dashboards that would have raised an early alert. This is being changed (see below).

Customer-facing remediation and commitments (what customers should expect):
- We rolled back the optimization immediately and applied a targeted patch ensuring invalidation messages are emphatically delivered (commit PR #4521).
- Within 72 hours we will deploy an additional safety layer: a sequence-number based check between frontends and workers for session-affine KV caches. This prevents workers from serving state older than a known session generation. (ETA: 2027-03-05 23:59 UTC)
- We will add a status metric (Cache Invalidation Miss Rate) to the public status page and the account-level console within 7 days.
- For customers who need immediate stronger guarantees, we have a recommended configuration: pin requests to region-local pools (instructions below) and enable strict-session-affinity flag on Dedicated/Private deployments; we will assist staffed account teams in applying these settings.

Suggested immediate customer actions (if you observed problems):
- If you saw incorrect outputs: retry the affected interactions once from your client after 02:45 UTC (server returns the new retry guidance). Avoid automated rapid retries (backoff recommended).
- If you rely on strict deterministic generation for billing-critical paths: consider temporarily pinning to a single model shard/region using the console route override until our sequence-number safety is in place. Contact your CSM and we will apply for you.

Compensation and account-level support:
- We recognize this impacted reliability. For customers demonstrably affected (we will correlate request IDs/timestamps), we will grant a 5% credit applied to the next billing cycle, plus dedicated engineering support to review logs and suggested config changes.
- To request an account review, open a ticket referencing RWI-2981 and include example request IDs and timestamps; your CSM will coordinate.

Timeline (detailed):
- 2027-03-01 22:05 UTC — deploy of cache invalidation optimization (feature branch merged).
- 2027-03-01 22:30 UTC — first customer report from an EU customer: inconsistent outputs noted.
- 2027-03-01 22:45–23:50 UTC — sporadic reports; internal SRE/serving team paged; initial investigation points to KV mismatch patterns.
- 2027-03-02 01:10 UTC — rollback of optimization across both regions.
- 2027-03-02 02:00 UTC — cross-region routing temporarily disabled for affected latency-optimized routes.
- 2027-03-02 02:45 UTC — conservative retry behavior enabled and status page published.
- 2027-03-02 06:15 UTC — incident declared mitigated; monitoring remained stable.

Longer-term fixes and process changes (what we will do to prevent recurrence):
- Instrumentation: add Cache Invalidation Miss Rate and Session Generation Skew metrics to internal and public dashboards (ETA: 7 days).
- Runtime: implement sequence-number session-check between frontends and workers to ensure no worker serves data older than the session generation (ETA: 3 days).
- Safety: add a deploy-time gating check for changes that reduce control-plane signalling bandwidth (feature flag-only if telemetry shows miss rate < threshold).
- SRE/process: update playbooks to include KV mismatch heuristics and to notify customers earlier when semantic divergence of outputs is detected.

What we still don’t know (open investigations):
- Precise distribution across instance types: initial results show a higher incidence on older x86 instances with memory pressure; we are validating.
- Whether particular customer traffic patterns (very short sessions with aggressive re-join) make this more likely; feature team to run focused tests.

Contact & next communications:
- Primary contact: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) and your assigned CSM.
- Engineering postmortem (internal) will be published to Confluence linked above; we will publish a customer-facing postmortem summary within 10 business days with detailed timeline, RCA and code-level changes.

Appendix: sample customer-friendly status page blurb (short):
- Title: Partial/Incorrect Responses from Inference (resolved)
- Incident: For a subset of requests we served stale session data which caused incorrect or truncated responses. Root cause: cache invalidation signaling regression in a recent change.
- Impact: Some customers saw incorrect outputs between 2027-03-01 22:30 UTC and 2027-03-02 06:15 UTC.
- Current status: Mitigated; optimization rolled back; additional safeguards in progress.
- Actions for customers: Retry once if you see inconsistent output; contact your CSM for pinning or account review.

Notes to internal (for CSM + support copy editing):
- Tone: empathetic, accountable, practical. Avoid technical jargon in external summary.
- Attachment: include a small troubleshooting checklist for support agents with how to find request IDs, trace links, and example logs in the console (we will create as a separate doc).
- Follow-up: ensure customers receiving credits are tagged and billing notifications go out automatically.

Draft sign-off checklist (who needs to approve before publish):
- eng-sre: Diego Martinez (confirm monitoring changes applied)
- serving-runtime: Claire Nguyen (confirm rollback and patch PR merged)
- legal/security: Samir Rao (confirm no data exposure)
- head of customer-success: schedule final distribution

End of draft.

(Notes: keep this file as the primary customer-facing draft for RWI-2981 communications. Will iterate after engineering merges additional telemetry changes.)
